question.text: A comprehensive retirement plan review should include all of the following EXCEPT:

answer.text: Checking actual investment returns against planned assumptions
Updating the retirement goal based on changed personal circumstances
Predicting exact future stock market returns for the next 10 years
Reassessing risk tolerance as the client ages and circumstances change

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 3.6 calls for a review schedule, such as annual, and for reviews of changed circumstances, risk tolerance, investment strategy, inflation, expected returns and portfolio performance. Predicting exact future stock-market returns over a long horizon is not one of these review activities. The Trap: The other options are all part of the review checklist; only the claim of forecasting exact long-horizon market returns falls outside what a retirement-plan review can responsibly do. Note: The review is framed around updating needs, lifecycle and life-event changes plus revisiting strategy and performance, rather than around any specific multi-question framework.
